newsitem.title: INDIA: Motorola, IBM said seeking fresh India investments.
newsitem.headline: Motorola, IBM said seeking fresh India investments.

text.p: U.S. firms International Business Machines Corp and Motorola Inc have shown interest in making fresh investments in India, the chief minister of the southern state of Karnataka said on Monday.

J.H. Patel, who returned on Monday after a 15-day tour of the United States and Britain to scout for investments, told reporters the two firms had proposed to invest a combined two billion rupees ($56 million) in the state.
The two computer firms already have investments in Bangalore, the state capital.

"IBM wants to expand and are planning to set up a regional service base in Bangalore with a likely investment of one billion rupees ($28 million). Motorola has expansion plans worth one billion rupees for software," Patel said.
Patel said his state was in negotiations with British and U.S. investors for several projects involving a total investment of 22.65 billion rupees ($632 million).

Patel mentioned other proposed investments including 1.5 billion rupees ($41.8 million) by U.S. soft drinks giant PepsiCo Inc and 800 million rupees ($22.3 million) by an affiliate of Raytheon Company.

Anglo-French consortium GEC Alsthom, which has an Indian venture, GEC Alsthom India, had shown interest in investing 1.5 billion rupees in a transport component project with state-run Bharat Earth Movers Ltd (BEML), Patel said.
